goal.current: Locate the first failed branch in the ASUS-DEG2 control/message flow, identify its owning component and an observable that distinguishes it, then select one reversible intervention with a predicted outcome.
goal.eventual: With the existing dock, GPU and cable, restore ASUS router/GPU enumeration and display output using a reversible Windows remedy, then verify reconnect and removal/rollback. No working remedy is established.

frontier: Observed boundary: ASUS reports attachment and PD/control activity, yet Windows does not enumerate the external router. The unobserved interval includes USB4 entry, board signal routing, electrical link establishment and the transition to router discovery. A missing router alone cannot separate those steps.

stages.name: 1. USB-C attachment and reported power/data roles
stages.asus: Attachment and PD reported; later Windows role correction.
stages.dell: Attachment reported; partner UFP by first PD report in control.
stages.missing: Raw CC/PD capability exchange, precise physical insertion time.

stages.name: 2. Windows-UCSI / ACPI / EC supervision
stages.asus: Normal commands complete; policy-only trial ineffective.
stages.dell: Working control without recorded SET_UOR; platform policy differs.
stages.missing: Meaning of private firmware state in the failing physical interval.

stages.name: 3. Controller USB4 discovery and entry/exit decision
stages.missing: Fresh discovery, entry request/reply and exit history; actual PD firmware identity.

stages.name: 4. Board signal path and electrical link establishment
stages.asus: DEG2 path unmeasured; peer link works in a separate control.
stages.dell: Usable link inferred from operational router/tunnels.
stages.missing: Per-port routing, retimer and PHY state during this failed pairing.

stages.name: 5. Windows USB4 router discovery and tunnels
stages.asus: External router absent at captured checks.
stages.dell: External router and working tunnels present.
stages.missing: Whether a usable physical link ever existed before failed/absent discovery.

stages.name: 6. GPU/output and ordinary USB fallback
stages.asus: No external GPU/output; USB fallback enumerates.
stages.dell: NVIDIA GPU bound; owner confirmed output.
stages.missing: A reproducible repair, followed by reconnect and recovery validation.

sources.warning: A saved 12:xx test-session snapshot; current_state is a historical JSON key, not live machine inventory.
342 unknown records in an earlier decode of the same ASUS ETL; all342 later decoded. This does not update any Dell decode count.

claims.statement: DEG2 enumerated a USB4 router and NVIDIA GPU on Dell; the owner confirmed display output.
claims.limit: The display confirmation followed recording. This establishes that pairing; it does not certify ASUS signal margin or identical platform policy.

claims.statement: ASUS formed a reported40Gbps peer link in a boot bookended by dumps containing retained updater targets.
claims.limit: Target state was not sampled inside the peer trace. A peer link does not test DEG2 compatibility or PCIe tunnelling.

claims.statement: ASUS and Dell initially reported partner DFP. Dell reported UFP by its first PD report; ASUS corrected the role later.
claims.limit: Different runs/platforms and power contracts. These are asynchronous Windows reports, not cable packets or proof that the role difference causes failure.

claims.statement: ASUS reported successful role correction while the external USB4 router remained absent at the recorded checks.
claims.limit: An early No result is not a terminal failure event. Missing enumeration does not identify whether entry or electrical training failed.

claims.statement: A controlled policy1 intervention suppressed the recorded Windows SET_UOR correction but did not make DEG2 enumerate; stock policy was subsequently verified restored.
claims.limit: One controlled pair. This rejects that tested intervention as sufficient, not every Windows remedy or every role-related firmware interaction.

claims.statement: The failed normal ASUS trace has10 Windows UCSI commands and10 terminal completions with no recorded CCI error/busy/unsupported.
claims.limit: Command completion establishes the captured control exchanges, not USB4 entry, wire Accept, routing or link training.

claims.statement: In BIOS314 the OEM table6 getter returns without producing a reply; its IT8853 identity getter returns literal constants.
claims.limit: This explains the diagnostic response timeout in that build. Live EC flash was not hash-matched; the literal identity is not an independent chip identification.

claims.statement: The EC flag gates the outer UCSI worker; vendor host command75 sets it and76 clears it, with other writer paths also identified.
claims.limit: No attachment-triggered setter or autonomous USB4-entry decision has been established. Commands75/76 are not UCSI opcodes.

claims.statement: The flag value during the failed physical attachment remains unknown; the attempted application access paths returned no value.
claims.limit: A candidate address is not a working reader. No live flag clear or physical-memory read was performed.

claims.statement: A continuously blocked UCSI worker is less consistent with the captured successful commands; a short pulse is still possible.
claims.limit: Crosses code and capture evidence. It assumes the reviewed EC implementation applies; it does not establish actual bit values.
claims.reason: The original outer gate skips the worker that services those commands. Repeated completions oppose that gate staying set throughout the exchanges.

claims.statement: The cached DEG2 USB4 status is Successful on Dell and NotAttemptedOrExited on ASUS.
claims.limit: A cached device report cannot distinguish skipped entry from later exit, or prove freshness, packet order or link-training outcome.

claims.statement: The actual cable discovery, Enter_USB/response history and subsequent entry/exit order have not been recovered.
claims.limit: Additional analysis of existing summaries cannot reconstruct an event never retained.

claims.statement: The updater target-lifetime defect is not established as the sole USB4 blocker.
claims.limit: Specific effects on DEG2 remain possible. The peer control is counterevidence to a universal blocker, not proof the defect is harmless.
claims.reason: Working peer traffic occurred between same-boot dumps with the retained target identities present.

claims.statement: The xHCI Device Qualifier descriptor stall occurred after the first no-router observation; reset succeeded and enumeration continued.
claims.limit: This identifies a later USB fallback event. It does not explain the earlier absence or identify a PD-wire error.

claims.statement: ASUS and Dell selected different reported PD contracts from the same advertised source profiles.
claims.limit: RDO values describe requested contracts, not measured power. Their causal effect is untested; forced power changes are not justified.

claims.statement: The Rp-only trial established no recorded attachment; the preconnected-startup trial still lacked a router/GPU.
claims.limit: These are separate cases. Rp-only did not establish its intended changed condition; cold-start collection began after sign-in and missed initial negotiation.

claims.statement: Matching14 copied Windows images narrows binary differences but does not establish identical runtime policy or exclude Windows involvement.
claims.limit: Copied-image equality is not equality of every loaded stack, setting, firmware service or operating condition.
claims.reason: The same comparison also records unequal platform policy and ACPI support masks.

claims.statement: The live IT8853 string and the connected OEM PDO timeout cannot be promoted into independent physical-chip identification or a clean port-mapping comparison.
claims.limit: Preserve the actual successful string read and failed request. The owner reported UGREEN insert/remove before DEG2 in that connected run.
claims.reason: Original EC instructions construct the string; the connected-run record explicitly marks the before/after comparison unclean.

claims.statement: No identified available Windows interface currently supplies the missing entry/exit history or validated routing-state observation.
claims.limit: Existing interfaces and helpers have been identified, but their applicability/readability/side effects are not interchangeable. This is an access gap, not proof software repair is impossible.

claims.statement: The original EC relay copies CONTROL and MESSAGE_OUT to controller-bus channel4/address byte98 and reads CCI/MESSAGE_IN back with acknowledgement.
claims.limit: This establishes a transport path in the reviewed image. Bus success, PD acceptance and private USB4-entry policy are not supplied by this code alone.

claims.statement: The single guarded SET_NEW_CAM EXIT request received a terminal firmware rejection; no successful exit or recovered router/GPU was established.
claims.limit: The error branch had no20-second passive window; immediate device state does not reveal internal mode retention. Do not repeat unchanged.

claims.statement: Recovered CPMUCSI AML exposes standard DSM command/status copies to and from the EC mailbox; it supplies no separate identified USB4-entry method.
claims.limit: An ACPI transport method is not the full controller policy state machine. Finding a method does not qualify an application interface to invoke it.

claims.statement: The public PS883x driver programs retimer mode/orientation overI2C; its USB4_CONNECTED configuration flag is software-written, not a measured usable-link result.
claims.limit: This is an upstream platform implementation. ASUS control-bus ownership, register framing and actual runtime state remain unqualified; the Qualcomm software quirk is not an ASUS finding.

claims.statement: ASUS returns CS18=00010400 with RouterDetected bit13 clear on both sampled passes; Dell deep control returns00003510 with that bit set and takes Yes. Both initially take Plugged No.
claims.limit: Matched read-phase samples with distinct logical adapters and capture times, not complete entry/link history or proof of never-ready state.

claims.statement: The pinned native Windows code tests ADP_CS_4 bit30 and USB4 port-capability CS18 bit13 from scalar configuration-read caches; its legacy TBT layout uses a separate branch.
claims.limit: Original instructions and exact PDB identities inspected; no new live requests or hardware-model validation.

claims.statement: The sampled Windows RouterDetected decisions follow the returned bit values; Plugged No alone is not sufficient to explain failure.
claims.limit: Upstream software programming/policy effects remain possible. These observations do not identify what prevented the ASUS bit from asserting or justify forcing it.
claims.reason: Clear native bit13 accompanies No on ASUS; set bit13 accompanies Yes on Dell, while both initially have Plugged clear.

claims.statement: The reviewed ASUS PS8830 ACPI devices expose eight400kHz I2C endpoints on I2CD; their DSM methods return constants rather than writing attachment-time mode registers.
claims.limit: Resource bytes verified in recovered original AML. Logical endpoints are not physical-chip count or connector ownership; other firmware/callers remain open.

claims.statement: Pinned Intel tbtools definitions identify CS18 bit16 as Wake on Connect Status, bit13 Router Detected, bits0..7 Cable USB4 Version and bit8 Bonding Enabled.
claims.limit: Reference field layout supplies names, not the history or writer of the ASUS returned value.

claims.statement: The saved ASUS CS18 sample has Wake on Connect Status set, RouterDetected/Bonding clear and cable version0; Dell has RouterDetected/Bonding set, wake status clear and cable version16.
claims.reason: Apply the independently published field masks to the already pinned native readback values.
claims.limit: A status bit and absent cable metadata do not prove an uncleared interrupt, missing entry, retimer error or a specific failed training stage.

claims.statement: ASUS attachment-time ownership of both APU crossbar and PS8830 mode programming remains untraced; TI and Infineon references motivate following the PD-to-APU and retimer coordination path.
claims.limit: Vendor reference architectures are not proof of ASUS implementation. No TI register/control value is qualified for ASUS ITE hardware.

claims.statement: The inspected BIOS314 IA32 TE USB4 PEI entry checks platform support, emits diagnostics and returns; the DXE manager is separately gated. Reviewed DXE ReadyToBoot/ExitBootServices bodies close their events rather than implementing PD mode programming.
claims.limit: These are original package code paths, not evidence of live execution, gate values, full firmware coverage or a startup repair.

claims.statement: AmdUsb4PortLinkConfigure in the reviewed BIOS module uses USB4 adapter configuration reads/writes for PORT_CS_19 FEC/reset and lane state; it is not an identified PS8830 mode/orientation I2C writer.
claims.limit: No retimer programming sequence recovered in this reviewed routine. Downstream port reset is not USB-PD entry and was not executed.

claims.statement: The selected modules and six standard bus GUIDs do not yet locate ASUS attachment-time PD-to-APU/retimer programming. A GUID dependency or a routine named link configure is insufficient to assign runtime control ownership.
claims.reason: Independent code inspection resolves the link routine to USB4 configuration packets and an OEM bus-GUID candidate to a notify/configuration callback. Positive protocol matches validate the bounded scan, not an exhaustive owner search.
claims.limit: Private protocols, direct IO, SMU/EC paths and PD-private firmware remain open. Actual ASUS writer and physical cause unresolved.

claims.statement: Dell records RouterDetected Yes, then successful lane0 CL0 polling, then CS19 PortConfigured changing0x40006 to0x4000e. ASUS records only two root-adapter CS19 writes in this retained log, both later sleep/wake programming0x40006 to0x10006 after the initial No.
claims.limit: Packet/read-phase association and write acknowledgements verified. Counts are retained-log scope, not complete physical/pre-capture history. ASUS lane-disable status before the initial decision remains unobserved.

claims.statement: The pinned native Port::WritePortConfigured changes CS19 bit3/bit4 in cache20a and calls the CS19 writer. The lane1-disable test uses a different cached CS1 field and mask4000; a DPR workaround predicate uses router flags.
claims.limit: Different controls and register spaces; legacy TBT differs. No live cache/flags read or reset occurred, and code presence does not establish the branch executed.

claims.statement: The later Windows PortConfigured write is not the original trigger of the earlier RouterDetected Yes in the saved Dell sequence. Router detection, CL0 polling and final operational-router presence are separate milestones.
claims.reason: The matched current CS19 read has configured clear after RD Yes and CL0 polling; its acknowledged bit3 write occurs afterward. ASUS failure predates its recorded wake-control changes.
claims.limit: This ordering does not prove all earlier hardware history, identify ASUS mode programming or qualify an early configured-bit/reset intervention.

claims.statement: The saved working ASUS peer rundown identifies root lane0 adapter2, both lane states2 and bonding1, matching the logical adapter number sampled in the failed ASUS-DEG2 run.
claims.limit: Historical peer result, not an equivalent DEG2 attachment or direct RD-bit measurement; UCSI connector mapping and complete entry history remain unqualified.

claims.statement: The USB-IF definition makes CS18 wake-on-connect status bit16 read-only and cleared on sleep entry, separate from current router detection bit13. A write-to-clear acknowledgement test is not justified.
claims.reason: The official register table explicitly assigns RO access and sleep-entry clearing; it does not assign software acknowledgement semantics.
claims.limit: Normative expectation only; ASUS conformance, actual sleep history and the cause of its clear RD bit remain unmeasured.

claims.statement: The retained native notification pump primes the software plug-state manager and registers a completion callback; GetLatestPlugStatus consults that manager.
claims.limit: Reviewed functions do not certify host RX handling or physical packet delivery; cached state is not a new CS18 hardware read.

claims.statement: Both saved ASUS initialisation passes report successful notification-pump start, ReadAndArm and cached unplugged after RouterDetected No.
claims.limit: This establishes software arming only. It neither proves no physical connect notification occurred nor identifies the PS8830 mode writer or a repair.

claims.statement: ASUS has four matched ring-to-topology PLUG records, all root adapters6/7, and none logged for failed logical adapter2. Dell has ten matched plug/unplug records, including root adapter1 after its recorded RD Yes. Both decoder summaries report zero lost events.
claims.limit: Internal display events are not DEG2 port events. Zero reported loss and observed message emission do not establish uninterrupted enablement or complete physical event generation/history.

claims.statement: The retained host code separates ring size validation/logging, deferred OnPlugPacket callback dispatch and topology receipt before adapter lookup/client dispatch. The ring and topology logs use different gates.
claims.limit: Reviewed code scope, not complete transport validation or proof that a particular final client callback completed. Symbols and packet fields do not identify a PS8830 writer.

claims.statement: A wholly dead ASUS host receive/topology notification path is inconsistent with the paired internal-adapter events. A valid DEG2 port2 notification dropped by Windows is not demonstrated, so notification interception/acknowledgement repair is deferred.
claims.reason: The same saved ASUS host logs ring receipt and topology handling for four packets but no adapter2 packet at either stage. Static code places these observation points before final client delivery.
claims.limit: Per-port or transient faults remain possible. This does not identify why RD stays clear or prove that the PD/retimer hardware failed.

claims.statement: The pinned EC bank2 address-byte42/channel1 candidate prepares two-byte register/data writes with zero receive length, staged initialisation and three desired/last-written cached control bytes. Only successful firmware transport returns update the last-written copies.
claims.limit: Static code, not a captured bus transaction, live target identity, physical acceptance or current stage/cache value. GPIO-like bit operations do not identify the controlled signals.

claims.statement: The address42 candidate is not yet a qualified PS8830 mode-control intervention; its numeric address and cached bit writes do not establish physical target or USB4 signal ownership.
claims.reason: The reviewed functions expose a staged register-write protocol and generic bit setters, but no validated chip/register identity, board connection or attachment-time execution.
claims.limit: Indirect routing/power/reset effects remain possible. This deferral does not prove the path is unrelated or that a Windows repair is impossible.

timeline_limit: T0 is the first recorded Windows attachment report in each run, not physical insertion. Different runs, platforms, power contracts and capture dates are explicit. These tables align software reports only; proximity does not establish wire order or causation. The earlier Dell control supplies the Dell timeline; the deep Dell dump supplies cached-state comparison.

hypotheses.statement: USB4 entry is skipped or refused during discovery/policy negotiation.
hypotheses.needed: A fresh entry request/response or an understood controller decision record.

hypotheses.statement: Entry is attempted but routing, retimer/PHY or partner compatibility prevents a usable link.
hypotheses.needed: Entry outcome plus per-port link/routing result; successful controls limit universal faults but do not exclude pairing-specific failure.

hypotheses.statement: USB4 entry/link starts briefly and then exits or recovers into fallback.
hypotheses.needed: Timestamped positive entry/link observation followed by exit/loss. Cached NotAttemptedOrExited cannot distinguish it.

hypotheses.statement: A usable link exists at some point, but router configuration/discovery fails before Windows exposes the external router.
hypotheses.needed: Link-ready evidence plus router/configuration transaction outcomes. No-router observations alone do not rule this out.

hypotheses.statement: Suppressing Windows role correction alone restores USB4.
hypotheses.needed: New causal evidence beyond the already completed policy-only trial before reopening.

hypotheses.statement: The EC blocking bit stays set and stops host command service during failure.
hypotheses.needed: A valid live observation correlated with the failed interval; one bit would still not distinguish all four main explanations.

hypotheses.statement: Retained updater targets universally prevent ASUS USB4.
hypotheses.needed: Pairing-specific causal evidence before any cleanup patch is presented as a DEG2 repair.

actions.name: Consolidate existing sources, cases and timelines
actions.information: A checked map of evidence, ambiguities and prior exclusions; no new handshake data claimed.

actions.name: Qualify an observation of the missing transition
actions.information: Find whether existing retained logs or an understood software interface can distinguish entry, link, exit or router-discovery failure.
actions.cost: Existing files and primary documentation first; no live requests authorized by this action.

actions.name: Build a dedicated flag-reader driver
actions.status: deferred; no longer default next step
actions.information: Answers a narrow host-service gate question; cannot reconstruct entry/exit or signal routing.
actions.cost: New kernel code, signing/loading and recovery burden; requires stronger benefit than present counterevidence.

actions.name: One shared read-only observer, if essential
actions.information: Several port-owned, understood fields in one capture; only after the returned values separate named explanations.
actions.cost: At most one proposed temporary helper; a loading/recovery plan and a useful positive control are prerequisites, not yet satisfied.

actions.name: Repeat a generic full dump or unchanged collector
actions.information: Does not supply already-missing controller-private history without a new capture capability.
actions.cost: Owner time, reconnection and possible system load.

actions.name: Repeat policy, mode-exit, table6 or cold-start tests
actions.status: not selected without a new discriminating condition
actions.information: Existing results already bound those exact attempts; more repetitions do not identify the missing transition.
actions.cost: Avoidable reconnections, boot or command side effects.

actions.name: Prepare a precise OEM logging/firmware question if software visibility ends
actions.information: Ask for the responsible PD firmware/decision log and validated read-only diagnostics, backed by the mapped failing/working evidence.
actions.cost: No machine change; depends on external documentation or engineering response.

corrections.explanation: The earlier ASUS summary says342 unknown records; the later analysis decoded those same342. That earlier decode-count field is superseded, not a reason to repeat decoding or claim Dell unknown records are also resolved.
The returned IT8853 string is real, but original firmware shows it is a literal build identifier. It does not independently identify physical silicon.
The connected OEM PDO run includes the owner-reported UGREEN insertion/removal. Preserve it as a failed read, not a clean paired port comparison.
The policy record has a historical key named current_state. It cannot establish current boot/security configuration; refresh live inventory only when a later action actually needs it.

The flagged EC worker and the normal Windows command completions belong to different evidence classes. Their relation is an inference assuming the reviewed firmware applies, not a measured flag value.

standards.title: Microsoft USB4 design requirements
standards.scope: The Windows USB4 connection manager has no software dependency on the Type-C stack; successful UCSI requests do not certify USB4 entry/link.

standards.title: Microsoft USB4 connection manager
standards.scope: Router detection/configuration, tunnel setup and domain management are distinct responsibilities.

standards.title: Microsoft USB4 debugging and troubleshooting
standards.scope: Existing trace, rundown and debugger mechanisms to audit before proposing a new observer.

architecture.scope: This is the bounded architecture/control-flow map, not a complete recovered PD firmware state machine. Branches tagged traced_code come from the reviewed BIOS image, whose live-flash match remains unverified. Measured edges describe software reports/outcomes. The private controller decision and board-to-host readiness path remain explicitly unmapped. Windows UCSI command completion and Windows USB4 router discovery are separate observation paths.
